correctness.rationale: PASS. RESULT.md proves for all integers k>=1 that the infinite gcd of k-term Pell cube windows is 1 for odd k and T_r*3^[4|r]/7^[3|r] for k=2r, T_r=P_r (even r) or Q_r (odd r). The normalization Q_0=Q_1=1, initial n=0 window and all prime powers are explicit. The Pell matrix identity M^(2r)=I+2T_r B with primitive integer B, Cassini congruences, and two-parity argument confine common primes; cubic polynomial A=-16x^3-3x^2 y+9xy^2-2y^3 satisfies A(y,x+2y)-A(x,y)=14x^3; telescoping gives 7S_n=T_r Phi_n with integral Phi, Phi mod T_r=3w(15x^3-9x^2y-xy^2+y^3). The n=0 valuation is exact for all primes of T_r except 3; at 3 the global extra factor is exactly one when 4|r, using Phi(0,1)=3w+t(18w^2-12)+O(t^2). The period modulo 7 gives exactly 3|r. Separately reconstructed the polynomial congruences with symbolic algebra and exact gcds for the first four windows for all k=1..100. The monic fourth-order cube recurrence explains why four windows determine the infinite gcd; the finite 100-case test is corroboration and not the infinite proof.
